title: Quantitative Timed Universal Simulation
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine code with canonizer, and let $\alpha,x$ be binary words and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. There exists a finite-state binary Turing machine $U$ such that, for every output word $y$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ at exactly time $t$ with output $y$, then $U$ halts on input $\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ at exactly time $(3|\alpha|+14T_c(|\alpha|)+50)(t+1)^2$ with output $1y$; and if it does not halt on $x$ with any output at exactly time $t$, then $U$ halts on that same input at exactly that time with output $0$. Here $T_c(n)$ is the canonizer's time bound at input length $n$, $\mathrm{bin}(t)$ is the little-endian binary representation, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the specified pairing of binary words.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine code with canonizer
For each output word, the decoded machine's computation at exactly time $t$ is considered
Either the decoded machine halts at exactly time $t$ with that output, or it has no output at exactly time $t$
